question: Why did the timed run land on an A40 rather than the recommended A5000?
answer: The A5000 was gone and stayed gone. Seventeen create refusals across the afternoon and three deep capacity probes ten minutes apart, all reporting Out on every probed CUDA version in Secure EU-SE-1. The pool is ten units and none came free.

per_gpu_read.caveat: this figure spans Community as well, so LOW here did not mean a Secure machine existed

operational_lesson: retry the create four or five times; use the deep probe to decide whether to keep waiting, but treat it as advisory -- it disagreed with the per-GPU read within minutes, in both directions. A volume pins the pod to its data centre, so fleet-wide stock can be irrelevant.
consequence: the A5000 pod-life and cost figures in the README are arithmetic from the A40 run's duration, not a measured A5000 run

retries.note: probed first, then tried anyway because a probe can lag the scheduler
after a nine-minute wait; the pool had not turned over

asked for a 3090 instead: refused, and get-gpu-type reported the 3090 availability NONE in Secure with no data centres. The 3090 and the A5000 share the AMPERE_24 pool, so when one is empty the other usually is.

asked for a 4090 instead: refused in EU-SE-1, and get-gpu-type shows its only Secure stock is EU-RO-1 (pool ADA_24, LOW). A network volume is data-centre local, so a 4090 there cannot mount the build cache; proving on it would mean a fresh fat build from a bundle, which is a ~12.5-minute job on a toolkit image at $0.89/hr.
after a twenty-five-minute wait; still nothing
seven further attempts at a half-hour cadence, every one refused

retries.probe: get-gpu-type Secure minCudaVersion=12.8: availability NONE, no dataCenters, 13.2 available:false
retries.note: first hourly cycle after the half-hour cadence was abandoned; probe and create agreed for once, both empty

retries.probe: A5000 NONE again; but A40 LOW in EU-SE-1 and CA-MTL-1, A6000 LOW in EU-SE-1 -- the AMPERE_48 pool recovered
retries.note: asked again nine minutes later. The 24 GB pool is still empty while 48 GB is obtainable, which is the clearest statement of the split yet: it is not the data centre that is full, it is AMPERE_24.

retries.probe_said: get-gpu-type Secure include=AVAILABILITY: availability LOW, dataCenters [EU-SE-1 LOW], 13.2 available:true -- a DATA-CENTRE-SCOPED read, two minutes before the first create
retries.note: the strongest instance of the catalog lying so far. Five refusals in two minutes: three with minCudaVersion 12.8, one with allowedCudaVersions [13.2] matching exactly what the read said was available, and one with no CUDA constraint at all. So LOW on the per-GPU read's own dataCenters array does not mean a machine exists, and this is a 48 GB card, not the contended 24 GB pool.
retries.correction: it retracts the AMPERE_48 'comes and goes, so the 48 GB cards are the ones that answer' reading committed in 2aa954f ninety seconds earlier. That rested on catalog reads; the create contradicts it for the A6000. What is actually established is weaker and duller: the A40 answered twice this morning, and nothing else has been obtained in EU-SE-1 since.

the_two_catalog_reads_disagree.observed: 11:40-11:42Z, minutes apart and in both directions
the_two_catalog_reads_disagree.get_capacity_fleet_wide_secure_13_2: NVIDIA RTX A5000: Low @ $0.27 (A40 and 3090 absent, i.e. Out)
the_two_catalog_reads_disagree.get_gpu_type_secure: NVIDIA RTX A5000: availability NONE, no dataCenters, 13.2 available:false
the_two_catalog_reads_disagree.reading: the fleet-wide grade is not data-centre scoped and can be stale or optimistic, and the per-GPU field includes Community; neither is authoritative. The create is the only test. A grade of Low elsewhere is useless when a network volume pins the pod to one data centre.

sharpest_instance.read: get-gpu-type A6000 Secure: availability LOW with dataCenters [{EU-SE-1, LOW}] -- scoped to the data centre, so not excusable as fleet-wide staleness
sharpest_instance.creates: five refused in two minutes, including one with no CUDA constraint
sharpest_instance.reading: a data-centre-scoped LOW is still not a promise. There is no read on this API that predicts a create. Budget for the create to fail and retry it; never schedule work on a grade.

the_binding_constraint.statement: the build-cache volume is in EU-SE-1 and a network volume is data-centre local, so the card choice is whatever EU-SE-1 has -- not whatever the catalog has.

EU-SE-1 on 2026-11-11.A40: Low at $0.59 at 11:00Z, NONE by 14:10Z, Low again by 17:47Z -- it comes back; the 24 GB pool did not
EU-SE-1 on 2026-11-11.RTX 4090: not present; its Secure stock is EU-RO-1 (pool ADA_24)

the_binding_constraint.consequence: $0.59/hr is the real floor for a cache-warm run today, so the measured 4 min 40 s / $0.046 A40 run is the honest headline and the A5000's $0.021 is a best case that needs the pool to be free.

unobtainable_window.checks: thirty-eight refused creates (thirty-three A5000, five A6000) and nine probes
unobtainable_window.reading: not contention but absence, for the better part of a working day, on Secure and Community alike. Ten units in the pool and never one free. The A40 answered twice inside the first hour, was NONE by 14:10Z and was LOW again by 17:47Z, so the 48 GB fallback comes and goes on a scale of hours while AMPERE_24 simply never returned; the only card obtainable in EU-SE-1 late in the window was the A6000, also $0.59.
unobtainable_window.what_it_means_for_planning: price the work at the A40/A6000 tier of $0.59/hr and treat $0.27 as a windfall that may not arrive for a day. A schedule that must produce a proof at a particular hour cannot rest on spot-style 24 GB capacity at all -- that is the argument for a committed box rather than a cheaper hourly rate.

catalog_snapshot.tool: list-gpu-types include=AVAILABILITY product=POD cloud=SECURE minCudaVersion=12.8 -- one call, and it carries each type's dataCenters array, which is the only DC-scoped read on this API
catalog_snapshot.caveat: advisory: the A6000 row below read LOW in EU-SE-1 and refused five creates in the same two minutes

NVIDIA A40.note: was EU-SE-1 + CA-MTL-1 four minutes earlier; EU-SE-1 dropped off

NVIDIA GeForce RTX 4090.note: moved: its only Secure stock was EU-RO-1 this afternoon

catalog_snapshot.everything_else: NONE, including the A5000, the 3090, the whole AMPERE_16 family, the L40/L40S, the RTX 6000 Ada and both H100 variants other than SXM
catalog_snapshot.in_EU_SE_1_where_the_cache_is: one card, the A6000 -- and it refused five creates

the_cache_is_not_arch_limited.fact: the cached build's key records cuda_archs 86,89,120, so the binary is fat across Ampere, Ada and Blackwell consumer/pro parts
the_cache_is_not_arch_limited.does_not_cover: A100 (80), H100/H200 (90), B200 (100) -- those would need a rebuild, and they are the wrong price for this job anyway
the_cache_is_not_arch_limited.so: architecture is NOT what stops us using the cheap cards on offer today. The network volume being data-centre local is. L4 at $0.59 in EU-RO-1, RTX PRO 4500 at $0.72 there and the A40 at $0.59 in CA-MTL-1 are all arch-compatible with the existing binary and all unreachable from a EU-SE-1 volume.
